backgroundScene: Lugh stands in the royal court of Avalora — a colossal hall of silver and oak where the Tuatha's many-skilled sovereignty is displayed. Enormous craft-tools of divine scale line the walls — smith hammers, harps, spear-racks, and artisan implements, each a monument to mastery. The Silver-Root Gate opens behind the throne dais, its silver-root geometry framing the gate's luminous threshold. Living oak columns grow from floor to ceiling, their surfaces inlaid with silver and sidhe-green. Lugh's spear is mounted in the center of the hall, its radiant glow illuminating the entire space. The scene communicates: he IS mastery of all arts — the court exists because excellence needs a throne.
scaleCue: The craft-tools on the walls would be gallery installations to humans but are hand-tools to him. The hall could hold a small city.
factionSkinLanguage: Living bark-silver skin with moonlit green-gold undertones. Thorn-vine patterns grow through the flesh like living tattoos. Fae glass fractures sparkle beneath the surface. Geas scars glow with silver-sidhe light. Mist-veil texture on the skin's surface — perpetually slightly out of focus, as if existing between mortal and fae. Root-lace patterns trace the nervous system in silver.
factionTraitDetails: Fae divine proportions — impossibly elegant, slightly elongated, with an unsettling beauty. The body changes slightly in peripheral vision — shapes shift, sizes seem wrong. Silver branch antler patterns can grow from brow and shoulders. Mist emanates from the skin continuously. The body feels ancient despite youthful appearance — thousands of years of memory in living wood.
